newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - March 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - March 14.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A Presidential committee yesterday upheld the contract between the Public Estates Authority and the Amari Coastal Bay Development Corp for the reclaimed Manila Bay property despite allegations of a payoff and tax evasion. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- Congress leaders promised the Palace yesterday that they will pass the third component of the Comprehensive Tax Reform Package before May 1. (TODAY)

- A ranking opposition leader said yesterday a proposal of the People's Initiative for Reform, Modernisation and Action to hold a plebiscite for charter change during the general registration of voters in June will violate the law. (MALAYA/TODAY)
- With the bleak prospects facing the sugar industry, property development beckons as an attractive alternative for many of Bacolod province's big sugar land owners. (TIMES)
- Victorias Milling Co said its creditors agreed to a repricing of the interest rates on its loans and a 90-day moratorium on principal payments. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- The Department of Finance yesterday opposed the proposal of the Central Bank to convert the 40 billion-peso special deposit of the national government in the bank into equity. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
